q: Which of these is one of the four functions of management?
r: Controlling
The functions are planning, organizing, leading and controlling.

q: Setting goals and deciding how to reach them is which management function?
r: Planning
Planning sets direction and the steps to follow.
w: Controlling compares results with the plan.

q: What does a middle manager typically do?
r: Carries out top management's plans and supervises first-line managers
Middle managers link top leaders and front-line staff.
w: Sets the company's long-term mission alone
That is mainly a top-level job.
Performs all of the entry-level tasks
Ownership is not a management level.

q: What is a manager's span of control?
r: The number of employees who report directly to the manager
It affects how closely a manager can supervise.
w: The size of the manager's budget
The length of the manager's workday

q: What is delegation?
r: Assigning tasks and the authority to complete them to others
It lets managers focus on larger priorities.

q: Which job is a top-level management position?
r: Chief executive officer
Top managers set the overall direction of the organization.

q: What is the focus of management by objectives?
r: Setting measurable goals together with employees
Progress is reviewed against the agreed goals.
w: Setting goals only for top managers

q: Which leadership style has a leader make decisions alone with little input?
r: Autocratic
The leader keeps control of decisions.
w: The leader invites input and shares decisions.
The leader focuses on serving others.

q: Which describes democratic leadership?
r: The leader invites input and shares decisions with the group
Team members take part in decisions.
w: The leader stays out of every decision
The leader rewards or punishes based on rules only
That is closer to transactional leadership.

q: What do transformational leaders do?
r: Inspire followers to exceed expectations through a shared vision
They motivate change and growth.
w: Manage only by rules and rewards
Vision is central to the style.
Leave decisions entirely to the group

q: Which describes servant leadership?
r: Putting the needs of team members first so they can do their best work
The leader serves the team.

q: Which trait is most closely linked to effective, trusted leaders?
r: Integrity
Followers trust leaders who act honestly.
w: Leaders must be able to decide.

q: A leader who steps back and lets the team make its own decisions with little direction is using which style?
r: Laissez-faire
The leader gives the group a free hand.
w: The leader would make decisions alone.
The leader would share decisions actively.

q: What does situational leadership suggest?
r: Leaders should adjust their style to the people and the situation
No single style works for every case.
w: One style should be used all the time
The theory is about matching style.

q: What is a stakeholder?
r: Any person or group affected by a business's actions
Customers, employees and communities are stakeholders.
w: This is not a general definition.

q: What is the goal of a win-win negotiation?
r: An outcome that benefits both parties
Both sides leave with something they value.
w: That is not a negotiation goal.

q: Which action best builds trust with a client?
r: Keeping commitments and communicating openly
Reliability and honesty build trust over time.
w: Promising more than you can deliver

q: Two departments disagree about a deadline. What is the best first step?
r: Meet to hear each side and look for a compromise
Understanding both views helps find a workable solution.
w: Choose the department that is louder
Volume does not make a view right.

q: What is professional networking?
r: Building relationships with people who can help each other professionally
Contacts can share advice and opportunities.

q: What is a service-level agreement?
r: A contract that defines the level of service a provider will deliver
It sets expectations for the relationship.
w: A statement of the owner's equity
It is not a financial statement.

q: Which is an example of an external business relationship?
r: A partnership with a supplier
External relationships are with outside parties.
w: A team within the same department
Two coworkers on the same shift

q: What is recruiting?
r: Attracting qualified candidates for open jobs
Recruiting builds the pool of applicants.

q: What is a structured interview?
r: An interview that asks every candidate the same questions
It supports fair and consistent comparisons.
w: An interview with no prepared questions
An interview done only by email
The format is not the issue.
An interview with different questions for each candidate

q: How does good onboarding help new hires?
r: They learn the job and the culture more quickly
A planned welcome speeds up success.
w: It removes the need for training

q: How is the employee turnover rate calculated?
r: Employees who left divided by the average number of employees
It shows how many workers leave in a period.
w: New hires divided by total sales
Total pay divided by hours worked

q: Which of these is an employee benefit?
r: Health insurance
Benefits are added to pay in compensation.

q: What is progressive discipline?
r: Consequences that become more serious for repeated problems
It starts with a warning and escalates if needed.

q: From whom does a 360-degree review gather feedback?
r: Managers, peers and direct reports
Several viewpoints give a fuller picture.

q: What is critical thinking?
r: Analyzing information objectively to make reasoned decisions
It involves evidence and logic rather than assumptions.
w: It is not about being negative.

q: What is the first step in solving a problem?
r: Define the problem clearly
A clear definition keeps the work focused.
w: A solution needs a clear problem.
Blame does not solve the problem.

q: When does brainstorming work best?
r: When people offer many ideas before judging any of them
Holding back criticism encourages ideas.
w: When only one idea is allowed

q: What is confirmation bias?
r: Favoring information that supports what you already believe
It can lead to poor decisions.
w: Changing your mind when new data appears

q: What is a decision matrix used for?
r: Comparing options against weighted criteria
It scores each option so the best can be chosen.

q: What does root-cause analysis aim to do?
r: Find the underlying reason a problem occurs
Fixing the cause prevents the problem from returning.

q: Which is a healthy way to handle stress at work?
r: Breaking tasks into steps and taking short breaks
This keeps work manageable.
w: Ignoring the work until the deadline

q: Which tool helps rank tasks by urgency and importance?
r: The Eisenhower matrix
It sorts tasks into four categories.

q: An upset customer is shouting at an employee. What is the best response?
r: Stay calm, listen and offer solutions
A calm response can settle the situation.

q: A team is overloaded before a deadline. What should its leader do?
r: Reprioritize tasks and redistribute work
This brings the workload back in line.

q: What is burnout?
r: Exhaustion caused by prolonged stress
It can reduce motivation and performance.
w: It is more than a short break.

q: Which is a good step when resolving a conflict between two team members?
r: Listen to each side before suggesting solutions
This helps both people feel heard.
w: Take the side of the person you like better
